newsitem.title: BELGIUM: TRACTEBEL SAYS HAS NO DESIRE TO BE BOUGHT.
newsitem.headline: TRACTEBEL SAYS HAS NO DESIRE TO BE BOUGHT.

text.p: Belgian utility Tractebel said on Tuesday it preferred not to be bought by another group.

"I have no desire whatsoever to be acquired. I believe that on our own we have the intellectual and financial capacity to realise our ambitions," chief executive officer Philippe Bodson told a news conference on 1996 earnings.
Tractebel is 65 percent owned by Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) .
After Tractebel's merger with its unit Powerfin , announced today, SGB's share in Tractebel will fall to 50.27 percent as a result of the issuing of new Tractebel shares to pay for the merger.
Bodson said he would welcome an equal partner, but not a dominant other shareholder.
He refused to comment on questions about the impact on Tractebel of a possible merger between SGB parent company Compagnie de Suez and Suez's utility unit Lyonnaise des Eaux .

He said he had spoken to Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene about a possible impact of a Suez/Lyonnaise merger on Belgian interests. Dehaene and other Belgian politicians had expressed concern that such a merger would increase an already strong French grip on Belgium's utility services sector.
Bodson would welcome any local Flemish group willing to take a minority stake in Tractebel.
